item.title: The moduli space of maps from hypersurfaces and its Goodwillie tower
item.description: arXiv:2610.28809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a moduli space of continuous maps from smooth hypersurfaces varying in an ample linear system. To study its topology, we construct a scanning map to an appropriate section space and investigate its effect on homology. Our main innovation is a general argument based on Goodwillie calculus and applicable to various moduli spaces of maps. Along the way, we compute the Goodwillie tower of the section space functor based at any retractive space.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Aumonier

item.title: Pontryagin-Thom, $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere, and principal quadratic divisors
item.description: arXiv:2610.29065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Segal computed $\pi_0$ of the equivariant sphere spectrum as the Burnside ring by a Pontryagin-Thom construction, transversality, and marks. We carry out the same argument in the motivic setting over a field $k$: the Burnside ring is replaced by the Grothendieck ring $A^u(\Gamma_k)$ of finite \'etale $k$-schemes decorated with a unit, the marks by the Dress map $d(L,u)=\mathrm{tr}_{L/k}\langle u\rangle$ into $\mathrm{GW}(k)$, and a Pontryagin-Thom map $A^u(\Gamma_k)\to\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)$ is shown to be surjective with kernel $\ker(d)$. This gives $\pi_0(\mathbb{S}_k)(k)\cong\mathrm{GW}(k)$ for infinite perfect fields of characteristic $\ne 2$ without Morel's computation. We then identify $\ker(d)$, by a reciprocity law on $\mathbb{P}^1$, as the group of principal quadratic divisors of rational functions, so that $\pi_0$ of the motivic sphere is the unit-decorated Burnside ring of $\Gamma_k$ modulo principal quadratic divisors. The transversality step is proved by an elementary "re-topping" argument.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Ormsby

item.title: Day Convolution and Homotopy Groups on the Pointed Homotopy Category of CW Complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.29239v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We freely enrich the pointed homotopy category of CW complexes over abelian groups and equip the resulting functor category with the enriched Day convolution induced by the smash product. After identifying the convolution unit and recording the coherence maps, we compute the convolution of the homotopy-group functors. For integers $n,m\geq 2$ we construct a natural isomorphism $\pi_n\star\pi_m\cong\pi_{n+m}$ induced by the external smash product; equivalently, the external smash product is the universal natural pairing of homotopy groups. Under this identification, the symmetry interchanging the two factors acts on $\pi_{n+m}$ by multiplication by $(-1)^{nm}$.
item.dc:creator: Abhiram Srinivas Yedathore

item.title: Nielsen coincidence theory for $(n,m)$-valued pairs
item.description: arXiv:2610.29274v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We define a Nielsen coincidence number for pairs of maps $(f,g)$ where $f$ is $n$-valued and $g$ is $m$-valued. The classical definition of the Nielsen number does not work in this setting, but we propose a theory where coincidence classes are allowed to overlap. We invoke a notion of multiplicity of a coincidence point, which indicates to how many classes it can belong, and we show that our Nielsen number is a homotopy-invariant lower bound for the number of coincidence points with multiplicity. We show a computational result in terms of single-valued lift factors, and using this, a Wecken property for self-maps of the circle.
item.dc:creator: Karel Dekimpe, Lore De Weerdt

item.title: Discrete homotopy of graphs and $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements
item.description: arXiv:2610.29690v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Discrete homotopy theory is a combinatorial homotopy theory defined for discrete objects. Barcelo--Severs--White conjectured that the homotopy groups of complements of $k$-parabolic subspace arrangements are isomorphic to the discrete homotopy groups of graphs associated with the Coxeter complexes. We show that this correspondence fails in general by giving a counterexample in degree two for the $4$-parabolic subspace arrangement of type $A_5$.
item.dc:creator: So Yamagata

item.title: Small covers and the Four Color Theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.29131v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a combinatorial proof that every simple convex $3$-polytope admits a small cover without using the Four Color Theorem. We also prove that the assertion that every simple plane triangulation admits a mod~$2$ characteristic function with at most five values is equivalent to the Four Color Theorem.
item.dc:creator: Suyoung Choi, Ringi Kim

item.title: Spanning bipartite quadrangulations in even triangulations of real projective spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.29737v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study spanning quadrangulations of even triangulations of real projective spaces, using the higher-dimensional notion of quadrangulation introduced by Kaiser and Stehl\'{\i}k. We prove that every even triangulation of $\RP^d$, where $d\ge 2$, admits a spanning bipartite quadrangulation. Moreover, such a triangulation admits a spanning non-bipartite quadrangulation if and only if it is not balanced; if it is balanced, every spanning quadrangulation is bipartite. Our proofs use coloring monodromy: its orbits yield bipartite quadrangulations, while a covering-space construction gives non-bipartite ones. %In dimension three, a bipartite quadrangulation can always be chosen to induce $K_{2,2}$ on each tetrahedron. More generally, we establish a sufficient condition for the existence of spanning bipartite quadrangulations on closed manifolds in terms of the monodromy action, and derive a consequence involving the fundamental group.
item.dc:creator: Kengo Enami

item.title: Rigidity of multisections to the universal cubic plane curve
item.description: arXiv:2607.14128v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the following question of Farb: For which positive integers n is it possible to choose n distinct points continuously on every smooth cubic plane curve? This paper is a continuation of the work of Banerjee-Chen. We prove that such choice is unique up to homotopy for n=27 (smallest open case), and does not exist for n=36k+18.
item.dc:creator: Jinwen Yao (Tsinghua University)

item.title: Hypergraphs on Riemannian manifolds and their double homology
item.description: arXiv:2608.00708v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, by constructing double homology for graded submanifolds of $\Delta$-manifolds, we study the double homology of hyper(di)graphs on Riemannian manifolds. With the help of the canonical projection $\pi$ from ordered sequences to their underlying unordered sets, we prove a commutative diagram of the double homology and a commutative diagram of the spaces of differential forms of hyper(di)graphs on Riemannian manifolds. Moreover, we give some relations between the fundamental group(oid)s of hyper(di)graphs on surfaces and the (pure) braid groups on surfaces by certain homomorphisms induced from $\pi$. As applications, we study the homotopy types of filtrations for packings and coverings of balls on Riemannian manifolds with hypergraph constraints, and we characterize regular maps on Riemannian manifolds by geometric realizations of the independence complexes and hypergraphs on the manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Shiquan Ren

item.title: Tiny and Unique: The Lubin-Tate Action at Height $p-1$ from the Minimal Curve with Its Symmetries
item.description: arXiv:2509.23428v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $p$ be odd and $G' = \mathbb{Z}/p \rtimes \mathbb{Z}/(p-1)^2$ the maximal finite subgroup of the Morava stabilizer group at height $p-1$. Inverse Galois theory produces from $G'$ alone a curve $X$, the unique curve of minimal genus with $\operatorname{Aut}(X) \simeq G'$; its ramification, its field of definition and its equation are consequences of the group, not choices. We prove a $G'$-equivariant equivalence between the deformations of $X$ and Lubin--Tate space, so that the Lubin--Tate action of $G'$ is the action of $\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ on deformations of the curve. The proof is a coordinate-free Kodaira--Spencer argument reducing to a single character count. The action becomes explicit: $G'$ acts through $\mathbb{F}_p \rtimes \mathbb{F}_p^\times$ shifting and scaling $p+1$ points on $\mathbb{P}^1$. From this we compute $H^*(G', \pi_* E_{p-1})$ and its Tate cohomology. One identity, $\pi^{p-1} = -p$, runs through every section.
item.dc:creator: Rin Ray

item.title: Cobordism, spin structures, and profinite completions
item.description: arXiv:2601.05706v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $M$ and $N$ be smooth closed connected aspherical manifolds with good (in the sense of Serre) fundamental groups $G$ and $H$. We show that if $\widehat G\cong \widehat H$, then $M$ and $N$ are cobordant and the signatures of $M$ and $N$ agree modulo $8$. Moreover, $M$ is spin (resp. spin$^\mathbb{C}$) if and only if $N$ is spin (resp. spin$^\mathbb{C}$). We consider some analogous results for compact connected aspherical manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Sam Hughes, Andrew Ng

item.title: Non-kinetic homotopy coherent actions on four-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.24548v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give the first example of a non-kinetic smooth homotopy coherent action of order two on a closed simply connected smooth four-manifold. This action is obtained by restricting a nontrivial smooth homotopy coherent action of the discrete circle group on a stabilized $K3$ surface. We also construct relatively non-kinetic smooth homotopy coherent extensions of boundary involutions over compact smooth $4$-manifolds. In addition, we exhibit boundary involutions that admit locally linear topological extensions but no smooth extensions over the same stabilized fillings. Nevertheless, we prove a Wall-type theorem showing that every free involution on a disjoint union of integral homology spheres extends smoothly over any simply connected smooth filling after sufficiently many stabilizations by $S^2\times S^2$.
item.dc:creator: Sungkyung Kang, JungHwan Park, Masaki Taniguchi

item.title: A nontopological triangulated category which is $\theta$-dg enhanced
item.description: arXiv:2610.25198v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every nonzero commutative ring $R$ and infinite cardinal $\theta$, we construct a nontopological triangulated category over $R$, whose thick subcategories generated by $<\theta$ objects admit $R$-linear dg enhancements, while the scalar action of $R$ is faithful.
item.dc:creator: Chencheng Zhang
